column5: Carpet underlay made from reclaimed urethane foam pieces. Source metadata describes 9 mm roll stock; this nominal stock thickness is identity metadata, not the instrument-measured sample thickness or a universal product specification. Exact scrap composition, binder, foam density distribution, blowing agent and manufacturer grade are unknown. No moisture, contact pressure, isotropy, compression-response, aging, strength, expansion, fire/degradation or service-temperature law is inferred from these thermal experiments.

The Dry condition follows the source's general preparation: oven at 105 degC for at least 48 hours with mass monitoring, then storage with Drierite desiccant. Exact residual moisture, pressure, foam aging and changes to cell structure are not measured here. Oven exposure is a conditioning history, not an operating-temperature range. The dry profile does not interpolate between drying histories or infer a moisture-transport law. The general conductivity method is ASTM C518 with through-thickness upward heat flow; the general capacity method is ASTM C1784-20 with equal-temperature plate steps. Applied contact pressure, calibrated instrument uncertainty, specimen-axis mapping and cross-property covariance are not provided. Conductivity and capacity are distinct runs; joint thermal use is conditional on treating the selected product/conditioning population as representative, not proof of identical coupons or independent measurements.

column5: The 3 complete native volume-capacity results are averaged at each source temperature. Temperatures round to 0.1 degC as in the primary reduction, giving 10,20,30,40 degC; conversion to kelvin adds exactly 273.15. Across-specimen sample SD is sqrt(sum((C_i-mean_C)^2)/(3-1)); it is retained as a discrete statistic, not a confidence interval or instrument uncertainty. Extra computed digits are arithmetic, not extra measurement resolution. Linear interpolation of mean C(T) and the published Cp(T) is an authored local approximation to finite-step estimates; interpolation error is unquantified and extrapolation is disallowed.

Rebond_Foam_Carpet_Pad_Density_Dry_R1.csv, Rebond_Foam_Carpet_Pad_Density_Dry_R2.csv and Rebond_Foam_Carpet_Pad_Density_Dry_R3.csv report densities 83,83,88 kg/m3. Corresponding masses are 34,33.6,21.2 g and volumes are 412,406.5,240.1 cm3. The primary reduction averages the reported rounded density column to 84.66666666666667 kg/m3; recomputing mass divided by volume would change that normalization. Density measurement temperature is not stated. This scalar is a reference normalization input without a temperature validity domain, not a measured density(T) curve or a constant density law.

The mean native volume-capacity values divided by mean reported density are rounded to whole J/(kg K): 1653,1665,1684,1724 at 10,20,30,40 degC. Published SD 43,42,41,43 J/(kg K) is native capacity sample SD divided by the same mean density and rounded to whole units. This does not propagate density scatter, covariance or calibration uncertainty. Cp, native C and normalization density are algebraically related, not independent measurements; the rounded published Cp values remain distinct from unrounded native C.

column5: 2 specimens each provide three repeated cycles at each mean temperature: 6 readings per temperature, not 6 independent specimens. Raw measured mean temperatures round to 15,45 degC. The primary script pools the readings, rounds means and sample SD to 0.001 W/(m K), and publishes means 0.037,0.041 with SD 0,0. A printed SD of 0.000 is rounding, not zero uncertainty. Linear interpolation between mean-temperature groups is an authored approximation with unquantified error. Only actual groups are retained; blank cells from aligned condition tables do not create measurements.

The thermal-conductivity curve requires mean-test-temperature-as-local-model=1. It explicitly substitutes the finite-gradient apparent HFM conductivity for a local scalar through-thickness coefficient at the same numerical temperature. This is an authored engineering approximation, not deconvolution of the 20 K plate difference, a point measurement or proof of isotropy. The apparent-thermal-conductivity curve retains its native test-mean-temperature axis.
